sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `extractMainColumn`'s "Comment" column never stripped `<i title="Primary alias">` before reading comment text, so on a row whose entity comment was wholly or partly a primary alias, the alias text showed up mislabeled as a disambiguation comment (e.g. artist-works' "An der schönen blauen Donau, op. 314" → Comment showed its alias "On the Beautiful Blue Danube, op. 314" verbatim — see debug/work-comment-bug.html). The two duplicated inline extraction blocks that built `MB-Name`/`Comment` are now unified into a single new helper, `_extractMainColumnParts()`, which also splits out a new third synthetic column, `MB-Primary alias`. The identical bug in the independent `_tagCountBase()`-backed extractor family (`Name_Comment`, `Name_Date_Comment`, `Name_Comment_Artists`, `tagCount_Name_Comment`, and friends — used by tag-value/tag-count page types) is fixed the same way.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Retired 7 `columnExtractors` entries using `extractor: 'primaryAlias'` whose `sourceColumn` matched their page definition's own `extractMainColumn` — fully redundant now that `extractMainColumn` natively produces `MB-Primary alias`. `tooltipColumns` references to the old `'Primary Alias'` column were updated to `'MB-Primary alias'` on those pages. The 3 page blocks that pair `primaryAlias` with the `_tagCountBase` family (no `extractMainColumn`) keep using it unchanged, since it remains their only source of alias data.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Same gap as WIP.67, for `release-group`-typed entity links (e.g. a report page's "Release group" column, `/report/SetInDifferentRG"` — see debug/rep-rg.html) — `_ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH` didn't recognize the `/release-group/{mbid}` URL path segment at all. Added `'release-group': 'rglink'` — note the CSS class is `rglink`, not a hyphenated `release-grouplink`; the map's key (URL path segment) and its value (CSS class name) are independently-confirmed facts about two different things, not derived from each other.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The unique-values dropdown's entity-glyph rows, and the new `name:`/`comment:`/`alias:` "Cell structure" filtering, silently did nothing for `release`/`recording`-typed entity links — e.g. an artist's "Releases"/"Recordings" pages, a label/series/instrument page's "Release" column, or an artist's "Relationships" page "Title" column. Root cause: `_ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH` (the map `_findCellEntityRefs()`/`_findCellEntityCommentParts()` use to recognize an entity link at all) only listed 6 of MusicBrainz's own glyph-marker types, based on an in-code comment claiming no `recordinglink`/`releaselink` CSS class existed anywhere in real MusicBrainz markup — confirmed WRONG via live page snapshots (`<span class="recordinglink">`/`<span class="releaselink">` genuinely render on an artist's Relationships page) and MusicBrainz's own icons stylesheet, which defines both (plus `serieslink`/`instrumentlink`/`rglink`/`collectionlink`/`genrelink`, not added here since nothing reported needs them yet). Added `release: 'releaselink'` and `recording: 'recordinglink'` to `_ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH` and corrected every stale comment repeating the old 6-type claim.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown's "Cell structure" section now supports filtering/highlighting by an entity's own anchored name, its disambiguation comment (excluding any primary alias), and its primary alias, independently combinable — e.g. an artist-works page's "Work"/"Authors" columns' `Name (Alias, extra text)` shape. Unlike the existing attr:/task:/date:/instrument: entries (which scan DOM sentinel classes this script injects when building release-tracks' bespoke AR columns), this works on NATIVE, unmodified MusicBrainz markup at query time — via a new `_findCellEntityCommentParts()` helper (extends `_findCellEntityRefs()`) reused identically by the counting pass, `_cellMatchesStructureMode()`'s new `name:`/`comment:`/`alias:` compound modes, and a new `_highlightEntityCommentPartMatch()` — so it works generically across every page/column with this shape (artist Works, report-detail, collection Works tab, search Works tab, and any other column sharing the same native markup), not just release-tracks. Scoped to entities that actually have a disambiguation comment; comment-less entities are unaffected (their name remains independently selectable via the existing href-based entity-glyph rows in the standard section).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown's quickfilter now also filters and `<mark>`-highlights entries inside the "Cell structure" section, not just the standard value list below it — typing narrows both sections together, and Escape/the × button clears both. New `_applySynBoxQuickFilter()` toggles visibility and rewrites each entry's own label span in place (synBox's entries are built once and keep their checkbox/checked state across keystrokes, unlike the standard list which fully rebuilds), and keyboard arrow-navigation now skips quickfilter-hidden "Cell structure" entries the same way it already skipped filtered-out standard entries.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: "Cell structure" section's count badges now right-align with a shared, panel-wide fixed width instead of their own unpadded natural width — symmetric with the standard value list's badges, and now the single source of truth for column-widest-count sizing across BOTH sections, so no badge in the whole dropdown can end up misaligned or overflow its column regardless of which section's number happens to have the most digits.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': unique-values dropdown's "Cell structure" section now surfaces the "Instruments" column's own instrument type (e.g. "bass", "guitar", "drum machine") as its own per-value checkbox entry, exactly like the existing per-attribute/per-task/per-date entries — one entry per distinct instrument actually present, checking one filters to matching rows and highlights the instrument link. `_buildInstrumentVocalsListItem()`'s cloned instrument `<a>` is now tagged with a new `mb-credit-instrument` sentinel class (its own href/click-to-instrument-page behavior untouched) alongside the existing `.mb-credit-attr`/`.mb-credit-date` sentinels, wired through the same `instrument:` compound structure-mode used for `attr:`/`task:`/`date:`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "Vocals"/"Instruments" columns rendered their attribute word (e.g. "lead") and date/task annotation (e.g. "on 1988-04-27") merged into one shared comma-joined parenthetical — "(lead, on 1988-04-27)" — instead of each in its own separate brackets like every other AR credit column (e.g. "Recorded at place"'s "(additional) (from 1987-01-20 until 1987-03)"). `_buildInstrumentVocalsListItem()` (the actual builder `_buildInstrumentsTd`/`_buildVocalsTd` share — a separate, less-developed twin of `_buildCreditListItem` that WIP.62's date-range "Cell structure" feature missed entirely) now appends two independent " (…)" parentheticals, symmetric with `_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd`/`_buildCreditListItem`'s own convention: "Bruce Springsteen (lead) (on 1988-04-27)". This also closes the gap that made WIP.62's date-range feature not actually work on Vocals/Instruments at all — the date/task annotation there was still a bare, unwrapped text node; it's now wrapped in `.mb-credit-date`/`.mb-credit-task` (via `_wrapDateAnnotationsInText()`/`_isDateAnnotationText()`) the same as every other AR credit column, so the unique-values dropdown's per-date/per-task "Cell structure" checkbox entries and highlighting now work correctly here too.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown's "Cell structure" section now surfaces AR credit date/date-range annotations (e.g. "on 1988-04-27", "in 1987", "from 1987-01-20 until 1987-03", and the bare "1988-04-27" shape special to "Recorded at event") as their own per-value checkbox entries, exactly like the existing per-attribute ("additional"/"guest"/"assistant"/"co") and per-task entries — one entry per distinct date expression actually present in the column, checking one filters to matching rows and highlights the actual date text. New `<span class="mb-credit-date">` sentinel (mirroring `.mb-credit-attr`/`.mb-credit-task`) is wired into every AR-credit builder that can carry a trailing date annotation: `_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd` (Recorded at place/Mixed at place), the "Recorded at event" bare-date cell, `_buildCreditListItem` (Vocals/Instruments/Performer/CREDIT_ROLES), and the generic `_buildKindSplitListTd`/`_buildLabelCreditListTd` (Phonographic copyright by artist/label, Produced for label, and any other AR column routed through the generic multi-kind-split builder) — the last two also correctly split MusicBrainz's own multi-date shape for a single credit (e.g. "in 1987, in 1988") into two separate date entries. Detection reuses the existing `_parseCreditDateAnnotation`/`_parseBareParenDate` date-shape recognizers from the live-recording-date-check feature, so both agree on exactly the same date forms.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values dropdown's "~ has name variation" Cell-structure entry only ever detected MusicBrainz's `<span class="name-variation">` shape (nested inside a relationship/credit list item, e.g. an artist's "Events" Location column or "Works" Recording artists/Authors columns) — it never detected the CELL-LEVEL `<td class="artist-credit-variation">` shape MusicBrainz uses on release/release-group listings' credited-artist column, so a genuine name variation there produced no entry at all. Replaced the three narrow `span.name-variation` lookups (counting in `openUniqDrop()`, `_cellMatchesStructureMode()`'s `'name-variation'` mode, and `_highlightNameVariationMatch()`) with a new shared `_findNameVariationElements()` helper that checks the cell's own class as well as its descendants, matched by class-name SUFFIX (`[class$="-variation"]`) rather than an enumerated list — generalizes to any current or future similarly-named MusicBrainz `-variation` class, page-type-agnostically, without a new hardcoded selector each time.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': every collapsable AR credit-role column (Recording engineer, Engineer, Producer, Mixer, Recorded at place, Recorded in area, Mixed at place, Performer, Instruments, Vocals, Phonographic copyright …, Produced for label, and any dynamically-discovered AR column) permanently lost its collapse/expand toggle and multi-row collapsed state the moment ANY filter was applied (typed text or a unique-values dropdown selection) — all their cells snapped to fully expanded with no way to re-collapse them, even after clearing the filter. Root cause: `_initColHeaderGlyph()`'s entity-type glyph marker (injected into these columns' headers only, via `_guardGlyphAgainstEmptySelectorHiding()`) embeds an invisible zero-width space (U+200B) that survives both `initCollapsableColumns()`'s glyph-character-class regex strip AND `.trim()` (U+200B isn't JS whitespace). On the very first render this is harmless (`initCollapsableColumns()` runs before the glyph gets injected), but every subsequent filter re-render reuses the already-glyph-decorated `<thead>` without rebuilding it, so `initCollapsableColumns()`'s own `th.textContent`-based column-name lookup permanently failed to match these columns by name, silently skipping their re-collapse step right after its own cleanup pass had already un-hidden every `<li>` table-wide. Fixed by switching that lookup to the already-existing, already-correct `_cleanColHeaderText()` helper (prefers the stable `th.dataset.colName` `makeTableSortableUnified()` stamped once, over a `textContent` re-derivation) — the same helper `_initColHeaderGlyph()` itself already relies on for its own idempotency check.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: WIP.58's "~ has name variation" filter never actually highlighted the matching `<span class="name-variation">` credit itself (e.g. "Nick Didia" on a release's "Recording engineer" column, or "Bruce Springsteen" on an artist's "Recording artists" column) — the checkbox correctly filtered rows but left no visual highlight on the matched name. Added `_highlightNameVariationMatch()` (mirrors `_highlightCreditValueMatch()`'s `attr:`/`task:` handling) and wired it into `testRowMatch()`'s structure-mode highlight pass. As a side effect this also fixes a multi-row cell's collapse toggle (▶N▤) never tinting to signal a hidden match when the matching name-variation credit was inside a COLLAPSED list — the existing `_COLLAPSE_MATCH_SEL`-based hidden-match signalling already looks for `.mb-column-filter-highlight` spans, it just had none to find until this fix started producing them.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown (📊): "Cell structure" entries (empty/single/collapsed/expanded/any multi-row cell state, title/name-variation flags, per-attribute/per-task credit-role values, and addCAA/addEAA inline-artwork presence) now get the same ☑/☐ multi-select checkbox behavior as regular value rows — checking one no longer closes the dropdown, and multiple "Cell structure" entries (and regular values) can be OR'd together within a column. Internally this folds the old single-select `dataset.mbMultirowMode`/`applyMultiRowStateFilter()` mechanism entirely into the existing checkbox mechanism via a new `MB_UNIQ_STRUCTURE_MODE_PREFIX` sentinel and shared `_cellMatchesStructureMode()` matcher — the legacy mechanism is fully removed, not left as dead code.
Unique-values dropdown: the column-header 📊 button's tooltip now mentions when that column also has a "Cell structure" section available to filter by.

Unique-values dropdown: entries with a glyph/icon (entity-type marker, flag/area icon, ▤ item marker on regular value rows; ▶/◀/✗/✓/≠/~/🖼️/∅ symbols on "Cell structure" entries) now explain that glyph's meaning in their hover tooltip — previously several of these glyphs (entity-type markers especially) had no explanation anywhere in the script.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: 'release-tracks': swapped which icon WIP.54's live-recording date check uses for each case, per explicit correction — a credit with NO date attribute at all now gets "⚠️" (was "❌"), and a credit whose date attribute DIFFERS from "Recording date" now gets "❌" (was "⚠️"). Only `_liveDateCheckResult()`'s two icon literals changed; the underlying missing-vs-mismatch detection logic, tooltips' wording, and the WIP.55/WIP.56 WARNING/ERROR summary buttons (which just tally whichever icon is present) are all unaffected.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': WIP.55's WARNING/ERROR summary buttons never appeared even when ⚠️/❌ icons were genuinely present on the page (e.g. real "Recording engineer" errors on /release/abc6ad0c-2e02-4141-8275-6943b3553dbf — see debug/h2.html) — both buttons existed in the DOM but stayed permanently empty and hidden. Root cause: `_updateLiveDateFlagButtons()` was only ever called from inside `updateFilterButtonsVisibility()`, and every one of that function's call sites is interaction-driven (`runFilter()`, editing a sub-table filter, "Load from Disk") — none of them fire on a plain initial page load with no user interaction, so the buttons were never populated after the first (and typically only) render. Fixed by also calling `updateFilterButtonsVisibility()` from the tail of `finalCleanup()` — the one page-type-agnostic function already called unconditionally once the initial render (single- or multi-table) is fully complete, as well as after disk-load. Also added `Lib.debug('filter', …)` logging to `_countLiveDateFlags()`/`_updateLiveDateFlagButtons()`/`_applyLiveDateFlagFilter()` to make any future issue in this area easier to diagnose.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': two new buttons in the "Tracklist" header, right before the global filter box — "(N) WARNING ⚠️" and "(N) ERROR ❌" — each only shown when at least one matching icon (from WIP.54's live-recording date check) exists on the page. Their tooltip breaks the count down by column (e.g. "Vocals (2), Recording engineer (1)"). Clicking one clears every other active filter and shows only the rows containing that icon, reusing the existing global filter/"Clear all filters"/status-display machinery, so clearing back to all rows works exactly as it already does for any other filter.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': for a live-recording track ("Recording of work" carries the "live" attribute) with a known "Recording date", each entity credited in "Recording engineer", "Vocals", "Instruments", "Recorded at event", and "Recorded at place" now gets a small ⚠️/❌ icon (native tooltip) whenever its own date attribute doesn't exactly match "Recording date": ⚠️ when it has a date but it differs (may be from a different performance), ❌ when it has no date attribute at all. Comparison is an exact string match, with no leniency for differing date precision. Deliberately excludes "Engineer"/"Producer"/"Mixer"/"Miscellaneous support"/"Performer"/"Produced for label"/"Mixed at place". New setting: "Flag live-recording credit dates that don't match 'Recording date'" (default on), depends on the existing "Recording of"/"Recorded at"/"Recorded in"/"Mixed at" columns setting for the "Recording date" data itself.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed the "Recorded in area" column header, and any area-typed entry in the 📊 unique-values dropdown (e.g. "Manhattan"/"New York" inside "Recorded in area"'s dropdown), silently rendering with no area icon at all — despite the correct `` marker genuinely being present in the DOM with MusicBrainz's own real background-image glyph correctly resolved (confirmed live via DevTools Computed panel: `background-image` resolved to the actual icon, but `display: none` won). Root-caused via a live DevTools Styles-panel walk (with the user) to a real, currently-installed third-party userscript's own injected stylesheet: `span.arealink:empty, a[href*="/area/"] > span.arealink:empty { display: none !important; }` — that script (a "More Flags Everywhere"-style enhancement) deliberately hides MusicBrainz's generic native area icon whenever the marker span is EMPTY, since it normally replaces it with a real per-area flag `` (which, once inserted as a child, makes the span no longer `:empty` and the rule stops applying). Our own glyph spans — both the column-header one (`_initColHeaderGlyph`) and the unique-values dropdown's generic per-entity-type marker (`_findCellEntityRefs`'s `glyphClass`, rendered in the dropdown's item-building loop) — are always genuinely empty (a header or a generic "this entity is an area" marker has no specific area to show a flag FOR), so they matched `:empty` too and got `!important`-hidden right along with the fallback icon they were never meant to suppress. MusicBrainz's own CSS was never the problem — confirmed via a separately-downloaded, unminified `mb-icons.css`: `.arealink`'s own rule is a plain, unscoped `background-image`, identical in shape/specificity to the already-working `.placelink`/`.eventlink`/`.worklink`/etc.

New shared `_guardGlyphAgainstEmptySelectorHiding(glyphSpan)` appends a zero-width space (`\u200B`) text node to any glyph span we create/clone ourselves — a text node with `data.length === 1` does not satisfy the CSS `:empty` pseudo-class's own spec definition ("no children, or only comment/processing-instruction nodes and zero-LENGTH text nodes"), so this reliably defeats the third-party selector while staying visually invisible. Called from both `_initColHeaderGlyph()` and the dropdown's entity-marker builder. Applied to every glyph class unconditionally (not just `arealink`, the only one currently affected) since it's cheap and harmless — a pure no-op for users without that userscript installed, since MusicBrainz's own CSS never keys off `:empty` at all — and future-proofs against the same third-party treatment being extended to other entity-type classes later.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed "Recorded at event" silently dropping its own trailing date attribute — e.g. the anchor text already spells out "1988‐04‐27: Los Angeles Memorial Sports Arena, Los Angeles, CA, USA", but the separate trailing " (1988-04-27)" sibling text right after the anchor (confirmed in `debug/double-ars.html`) was never read at all, only the anchor itself. Now found and appended the same way "Recording of"/"Recorded at place" already handle their own trailing parentheticals.

Fixed "Recorded at place" silently dropping an ENTIRE second place — reported live against https://musicbrainz.org/release/52c6808b-037d-47d5-b0c7-17331c9d36cd: a track with a separate "additionally recorded at: The Hit Factory…" `<dt>` AND a separate "recorded at: Thrill Hill East…" `<dt>` (two different studios during the same recording — NOT two places joined inside one `<dd>`, which was already handled) only ever showed the first. Root cause: `_findRecordedAtDt` used a first-match-only `.find()`, exactly the same bug class already fixed once for "Phonographic copyright (℗) by:" (see WIP.27) but never applied here. `_findRecordedAtDt`/`_findMixedAtDt` are now `.filter()`-based, returning every matching `<dt>`; `_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd` now accepts and merges the whole array into one cell, checking each source `<dt>`'s own "additionally recorded at:" wording independently (so a merged cell can correctly show "(additional)" on one dt's places but not another's).

Fixed "Recorded at place" (and, since it shares the same builder, "Mixed at place" — WIP.50) unconditionally DROPPING its own trailing date attribute (e.g. "(from 1987-01-20 until 1987-03)", "(on 1988-04-27)") — this was deliberate for the ORIGINAL "Recorded at place"-only design (no per-place date context existed), but is wrong now that dates are expected here too (see "Recorded in area", WIP.50, which already keeps its own trailing date). The date is now extracted from each source `<dt>`'s `<dd>` and re-appended AFTER the "(additional)" marker on every place `<li>` that `<dt>` produces, e.g. "The Hit Factory in Manhattan, … United States (additional) (from 1987-01-20 until 1987-03)" — matching the requested format exactly.

Fixed the 📊 unique-values dropdown's flag-icon decoration (WIP.29) not covering the new "Mixed at place" column (WIP.50) — it shares the exact same `_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd`-built `<span class="area-icon">`/`<span class="flag flag-XX">` shapes as "Recorded at place", so — like that column — this was purely a missing name-recognition entry in the dropdown's column allow-list, no new scan logic needed. "Recorded in area" needed no equivalent fix — its name already matches the allow-list's generic `endsWith('rea')` check.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed the "Vocals"/"Instruments" columns (WIP.46) silently dropping a credited artist's own trailing date attribute — e.g. "Bruce Springsteen (on 2002-08-29)"/"Toby Scott (from 1987-01-20 until 1987-03)" (confirmed against real data in `debug/therising.html`/`debug/double-ars.html`) rendered as just the bare artist name, date gone — spotted by comparing against a dynamic-fallback column ("Creative direction") built via `_buildKindSplitListTd`'s blanket-clone-the-whole-`<dd>` approach, which had ALREADY been preserving trailing dates correctly the whole time, unlike `_buildInstrumentVocalsListItem`'s selective artist-anchor-plus-known-annotations extraction, which never looked for one. `_buildInstrumentVocalsListItem` now also calls the existing `_findCreditSegmentTextAnnotation` (the same free-text-parenthetical fallback "Miscellaneous support"/bare-role CREDIT_ROLES columns already use for their own annotations) and merges its result into the SAME trailing parenthetical as the attribute words, comma-separated — e.g. "Jane Doe (guest/background, on 2002-08-29)" — mirroring `_buildCreditListItem`'s identical grouping. Deliberately NOT applied to the CREDIT_ROLES columns themselves (WIP.16 already established they drop trailing dates on purpose, and no regression was reported there).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed the dynamic-fallback AR-column machinery (WIP.48) fragmenting a single place/area "chain" credit into multiple columns and/or multiple rows — reported live: "Mixed at place"/"Mixed at area" split "A&M Studios in Hollywood" into two separate columns instead of one (`<span class="placelink">`+`<span class="arealink">` both appearing as direct children of the same `<dd>`, per real markup — `_collectEntityKinds` correctly detected BOTH kinds present, but `_buildKindSplitListTd`'s marker-boundary check unconditionally treated ANY of `KNOWN_ENTITY_LINK_KINDS`'s 7 classes as a segment boundary, regardless of what the caller actually asked to split by), and "Recorded in" showed only "Asbury Park" instead of the full "Asbury Park, New Jersey, United States (on 2002-09-20)" chain (an area's OWN parent-area ancestry legitimately reuses the SAME `arealink` marker class repeatedly — a fundamentally different shape from place-vs-area, where marker-KIND alone can no longer distinguish "the credited target" from "its own decoration"). New `PEER_SPLIT_KINDS` (`['artist', 'label']` — the only two kinds ever proven to have genuine multiple-PEER-entity semantics, e.g. `_buildPhonographicCopyrightTds`'s mixed artist+label case) restricts `_buildKindSplitListTd`'s boundary detection to markers the CALLER's own `kinds` parameter actually requested — any other recognized-but-unrequested kind marker is now left as ordinary content instead of fragmenting the segment. The dynamic-fallback discovery scan now filters its collected kinds through `_filterPeerKinds` before ever calling `_splitColumnByEntityKind`/`_buildKindSplitListTd`, so a place/event/work/area/series-shaped role safely falls back to `_buildKindSplitListTd`'s existing `kinds.size === 0` "clone whole `<dd>` verbatim, one row" behavior — never fragments — protecting any FUTURE unknown relationship shaped this way, not just the two observed cases.

Added "Mixed at place" (new `_findMixedAtDt`, reusing `_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd` as-is — same place-primary/area-decoration shape as the existing "Recorded at place") and "Recorded in area" (new `_findRecordedInDt`/`_buildRecordedInAreaTd` — cardinality-1 per MusicBrainz's own relationship-type metadata, so no segmentation is attempted at all: only the very first `arealink` marker is dropped, everything else — the full ancestor-area chain, flags, AND the trailing date — is cloned verbatim into one row) as their own DEDICATED fixed handlers rather than relying on the generic dynamic-fallback path, so they get exactly the chain-preserving treatment "Recorded at place" already has. `_dtMatchesAnyFixedHandler`/`_classifyArDt` updated to recognize both (plus a bare "performer:" — see the Feature entry below) so none of the three can be shadowed by a duplicate auto-discovered dynamic column.

Wired up the missing column-header relationship glyph icons (`_initColHeaderGlyph`) for "Instruments"/"Vocals"/"Performer" (all `artistlink`), "Recorded in area" (`arealink`), and "Mixed at place" (`placelink`) — these five new/WIP.46 columns never got the same post-render glyph re-injection every other release-tracks AR column already receives from `renderGroupedTable()`'s tail, so their headers showed no icon at all (confirmed via a side-by-side screenshot comparison against "Recording engineer"/"Mixer"/etc., which do). New `_glyphClassForDynamicColumn`/`def.features._dynamicArColumnGlyphs` runtime registration (mirroring the existing runtime `collapsableColumns` registration mechanism) extends the same glyph re-injection to dynamically-discovered fallback columns too, whenever exactly one entity kind is present for that role.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': added a dedicated "Performer" column (each track's bare "performer:" relationship, via the existing `_findCreditDts`/`_buildCreditListTd` machinery, no attribute-word prefix), positioned before "Vocals"/"Instruments" rather than lumped in with the CREDIT_ROLES columns — its own gate/setting reuses `sa_enable_release_tracks_credit_role_columns`.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: 'release-tracks': reordered the release-tracks AR columns to the requested final sequence: Recording of work, Recording date, Recorded at event, Recorded at place, Recorded in area, Performer, Vocals, Instruments, Recording engineer, Engineer, Producer, Mixer, Miscellaneous support, Mixed at place, Phonographic copyright (℗) by artist/label, Produced for label, [dynamic-fallback columns], ARs — swapping Vocals before Instruments (previously Instruments-then-Vocals), and reordering `CREDIT_ROLES` to Recording engineer/Engineer/Producer/Mixer/Miscellaneous support (previously …/Mixer/Engineer/Producer/…) so "Mixer" sits immediately before the new "Mixed at place". The whole header-insertion block now computes its shared "ARs" `<th>` reference ONCE (`_arsHeaderRef`) instead of four separate, identically-computed copies — the final column order is simply the order the insertion blocks now run in, following this same shared reference throughout.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': every AR relationship type not already covered by a dedicated column (Recording of/date, Recorded at event/place, the credit-role columns, Phonographic copyright, Produced for label, Instruments/Vocals — WIP.45-47) now gets its own auto-discovered column instead of only ever surfacing as raw text inside "ARs" — e.g. "Conductor", "Publisher", "Mixed at", "Lyricist and composer", "Creative direction", "Shot at", "Version of", "Concertmaster" (all observed in `debug/therising.html`/`debug/double-ars.html`), and any relationship type MusicBrainz adds in the future, with zero code changes needed. New `_classifyArDt(dt)` is the single source of truth for what kind of relationship a given `<dt>` is — checked in priority order: an already-handled fixed column (`_dtMatchesAnyFixedHandler`, covering everything above via the same `roleWords`/`_creditDtMatch` machinery those columns already use, plus the "recording of:"/"recorded at:" text+glyph checks), then Instruments/Vocals (`_parseInstrumentVocalsDt`), then the dynamic fallback — used by both the page-wide discovery scan and the per-row `<td>` builder so the two always agree. A page-wide scan (mirroring the existing `_pageHasCopyrightByArtist`-style gates) buckets every track's unclaimed `<dt>`s into a `Map<key, {displayName, kinds}>` keyed on the relationship's own literal phrase text (lowercased, trailing ":" stripped) — so e.g. "strings arranger:" and "cello arranger:" become two distinct columns, never merged, matching the confirmed keying decision — with the display name sentence-cased from the same text. Map insertion order (first-encountered-in-page) becomes the final left-to-right column order, inserted as a block right after "Produced for label", before "ARs": reading order becomes curated specific columns → auto-discovered generic columns → full raw ARs. Each discovered column can itself split by entity kind via the WIP.47 `_splitColumnByEntityKind`/`_buildKindSplitListTd` machinery (e.g. a hypothetical role crediting both an artist and a place on the same release). Gated by a new dedicated setting, `sa_enable_release_tracks_dynamic_ar_columns` (default on), independent of every other release-tracks column setting, since this is the most exploratory/unpredictable piece of the feature. Dynamically-discovered column names are pushed into `def.features.collapsableColumns` at creation time (dedup-guarded) rather than pre-declared in the page definition, since `initCollapsableColumns()` only matches by exact header-text string and the set of names isn't known at authoring time — `def` is the same object as `activeDefinition`, so this registration is visible by the time `initCollapsableColumns()` actually runs. Verified via a standalone jsdom-free unit test covering every previously-unhandled phrase above, plus regression checks confirming "live recording of:", "assistant engineer:", "producer and mixer:", "phonographic copyright (℗) by:", and "produced for:" all still classify as already-fixed (never shadowed by a duplicate dynamic column), and that a "strings arranger:" `<dt>` — rejected by the Instruments parser (WIP.46) specifically because "arranger" isn't a recognized attribute word — correctly falls through to become its own "Strings arranger" dynamic column instead of silently vanishing.

items: The 📊 unique-values dropdown now offers a fourth entry category: one checkbox per distinct MusicBrainz ENTITY REFERENCE (work/place/area — including country, which MusicBrainz models as just another area — artist/label/event) found anywhere inside a cell, marked with that entity type's own MB glyph (`worklink`/`placelink`/`arealink`/`artistlink`/`labellink`/`eventlink` — the same classes `_initColHeaderGlyph()` already reuses for release-tracks column headers). Generalizes well beyond the "▤" per-`<li>`-item feature (WIP.43): it applies to ANY cell — list or not — and surfaces sub-parts of a single value, e.g. "Recorded at place" (`debug/expand.html`, `/release/52c6808b-037d-47d5-b0c7-17331c9d36cd`): "The Hit Factory in Manhattan, New York, New York, United States (from … until …) (additional)" now offers the place, each area, AND the country as five INDEPENDENTLY selectable/filterable/highlightable entries, instead of only the one giant flattened string. "Recording engineer"/"Phonographic copyright (℗) by artist" similarly offer the bare credited artist's name (e.g. "Toby Scott", "Bruce Springsteen"), letting a filter match regardless of the trailing date range/year annotation. Keyed by the entity's own href/MBID (`MB_UNIQ_ENTITY_HREF_PREFIX`, sibling to WIP.43's `MB_UNIQ_ITEM_VALUE_PREFIX` in the same `dataset.mbUniqValues` checked-value set) rather than by display text — required for correctness, since the same entity can legitimately render under different alias text (a name-variation credit) and two different entities can otherwise share the same display text.

New shared `_findCellEntityRefs(cell)` (single source of truth for collection, matching, AND highlighting — unlike a naive implementation, this avoids three separate re-implementations of the same DOM-walk) finds every ``+`` pair in a cell, in EITHER nesting direction (`…`, the common case, or `…`, MusicBrainz's plain native "Artist" column). Deliberately never requires a glyph span to be present for detection: this script's own cell builders strip the glyph from a column's own PRIMARY entity (already shown once in the column header), so `href`+`` is the only reliable signal — confirmed against `debug/expand.html`'s real markup, where "Recorded at place"'s country entity uses a THIRD, different glyph shape again (`` WRAPPING the anchor, vs. every other area's plain empty SIBLING ``).

An entity only gets offered as its own entry when it's part of something bigger than just its own name in at least one occurrence (`ref.isBare`, computed by comparing the nearest containing `<li>`/cell's cleaned text against the bare entity name) — replaces any raw row-count threshold, and for free correctly skips a column whose cell is ALWAYS just the bare entity (e.g. "Recording of work"'s non-list cell, or MusicBrainz's plain `<bdi><a>` "Artist" column — both would otherwise just duplicate the existing whole-cell entry with an identical row-set) while still offering one for every entity in a chain or with a trailing annotation. `testRowMatch()`'s value-set filter gains a third, href-membership fallback (`f.hasEntityValues`, mirroring WIP.43's item-membership fallback's cheap-phase-1/expensive-phase-2 shape) attempted only after the cheaper whole-cell and item checks both miss. Checking an entity entry highlights ONLY its resolved name node (e.g. just "United States", never "Manhattan"/"New York"/"The Hit Factory" in the same chain) via the existing `_buildFuzzyTextMatchRegex()`/`highlightCrossTag()` — reused as-is, no new fuzzy-matching logic needed. Verified end-to-end in an isolated jsdom harness against `debug/expand.html`'s real "Recorded at place" chain, confirming exactly one entity (the checked one) gets highlighted out of five in the same `<li>`, plus a full re-run of every WIP.43 regression case to confirm the `combinedVals`/`renderItems()` restructuring (now a 4-way merge: whole-cell / item / entity) introduces no regressions.

items: The 📊 unique-values dropdown now offers each unique `<li>` item's own text as a separate checkbox entry (marked with a "▤" glyph) for multi-row (≥2-item) list-cell columns, e.g. "Engineer" (`debug/multi-row-cell.html`: "Billy Bowers (US engineer) (additional)" and "Karl Egsieker (task: Second Engineer)" now each get their own entry, alongside the existing merged whole-cell value) — lets you filter to just the rows crediting one specific person even when they usually appear alongside others in a merged cell. Multi-select, OR'd, panel stays open — same interaction as today's plain values; item entries are stored in the same `dataset.mbUniqValues` checked-value set as whole-cell values, distinguished by a reserved-prefix encoding (`MB_UNIQ_ITEM_VALUE_PREFIX`) so no new dataset attribute or restore-on-reopen plumbing was needed. Scoped purely structurally (`_findCellListItems(cell).length >= 2`, the same threshold `_classifyCollapseCell()`'s own "isMultiRow" already uses) rather than to any specific column list, so it works generically on every list-cell column, not just credit-role ones — and correctly excludes single-item cells (whose one item is already the existing whole-cell entry) and Annotation/prose cells (no `<li>`s at all). `testRowMatch()`'s value-set filter falls back to per-`<li>` membership testing only when a checked item entry is actually present, so ordinary whole-cell filters pay zero extra cost.

Checking an item entry highlights the exact matching `<li>` (unlike whole-cell value matches, which are deliberately never highlighted). Building this exposed a real, previously-latent bug: `getCleanColumnText()` (used to compute the checkable value) normalizes whitespace across DOM-node boundaries and strips paren-adjacent spaces, while `highlightCrossTag()` (used to paint the highlight) matches against the RAW, un-normalized text — for any value spanning more than one element (which every credit `<li>` does: artist `<a>`, `<span class="comment">`, `<span class="mb-credit-attr">`/`<i class="mb-credit-task">` are all separate nodes), a literal escaped-string regex silently failed to match at all. New `_buildFuzzyTextMatchRegex()` reverses `getCleanColumnText()`'s specific whitespace/paren-space transformations into a tolerant regex so cross-node highlighting actually lands. Confirmed against the real Karl Egsieker `<li>` in an isolated jsdom harness — its raw DOM text is `"Karl Egsieker
	 (
      task: Second Engineer
      )
    "`, nothing like the cleaned, single-spaced value a naive literal-match regex would have required.

Fixed a second, harder case of the same cross-node-highlight problem, reported live: "Roger Talkov (engineer) (assistant)" checked and correctly filtering, but rendering with zero highlight anywhere in the `
  • ` (a sibling "Tim Leitner (assistant)" entry in the same cell highlighted fine). Root cause: the first fix's regex used `\s+` (one-or-more) for each normalized space, assuming a real raw whitespace character always exists at that boundary — but `…Roger Talkov (engineer)` connects the artist name to its disambiguation comment via an ISOLATED ` ` text node, which `.trim()`s to empty (non-breaking space IS whitespace) and is therefore entirely `FILTER_REJECT`ed by `highlightCrossTag()`'s own walker — contributing ZERO characters to the raw text being matched, not even one whitespace char, so the mandatory `\s+` failed outright. `_buildFuzzyTextMatchRegex()` now uses `\s*` (zero-or-more) for every normalized space instead, correctly covering both "real whitespace bridges this gap" and "the only bridging node was itself whitespace-only and vanished entirely". Verified against the actual live DOM captured from https://musicbrainz.org/release/52c6808b-037d-47d5-b0c7-17331c9d36cd's Engineer column, plus a full re-run of every earlier regression case (Billy Bowers/Karl Egsieker, both checked simultaneously) to confirm no loss of precision from the looser `\s*`.

items: 'release-tracks': fixed column/global filter highlighting silently never appearing on the "Length" column specifically (`debug/no-color.html`) — reproduced end-to-end in an isolated jsdom harness against the real extracted `testRowMatch()`/`highlightText()`/`highlightCrossTag()` code, which proved the highlight mechanism itself is correct; the wipe happens one step later. Root cause: jesus2099's "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL" userscript mutates the native Length `<td>` in place, setting `class="treleases"` (see `_repairTreleasesTd()`'s own JSDoc and `debug/tracklist-single-medium.html`, which shows this class co-occurring with jesus2099's own toolzone `<div>`s on a real page). The existing `'jesus2099-any'` columnEraser (WIP.2) already strips those nested toolzone/editbutt/openEdits `<div>`s from the Length column at scrape time, but never touched the `treleases` class living on the `<td>` itself — so it survived into this script's own captured row and every future `cloneNode(true)` copy of it. `runFilter()`'s multi-table path clones from that captured row on every keystroke and inserts the clone into a fresh `<tbody>`; `initTreleasesObserver()`'s `MutationObserver` cannot distinguish that routine self-triggered insertion from a genuine live jesus2099 mutation, so it fired `_repairTreleasesTd()` on our OWN freshly-highlighted cell — which rebuilds the cell from plain `textContent` (correctly preserving the visible "4:35" value and its numeric-alignment styling) but has no notion of the active filter, silently discarding the `mb-column-filter-highlight`/`mb-global-filter-highlight` `<span>` `testRowMatch()` had just added. Only the Length column is affected since it's the only column jesus2099 marks this way. Fixed by stripping `class="treleases"` (plus jesus2099's plugin `title`/inline `style`) from the cell in the SAME `'jesus2099-any'` eraser pass, once, at scrape time — this script's own rows are now permanently free of the marker, while `initTreleasesObserver()`/`_repairTreleasesTd()` still correctly react to and repair genuine future jesus2099 mutations on the live page, exactly as before.

items: Root-caused the "vzell" ISRC-filter injection via cross-browser testing with the user: reproduces on Chrome and Vivaldi, NOT on Firefox, Opera, or Brave — despite Opera/Brave also being Chromium-based, ruling out a generic engine quirk. Vivaldi is documented to license and use Google's own proprietary autofill/prediction backend (the same one Chrome uses); Brave and Opera implement their own independent autofill without it. Confirms this is Chrome's/Vivaldi's NATIVE, built-in credential-autofill — which has a long-standing, deliberate policy (crbug.com/468153) of ignoring `autocomplete="off"` for anything its heuristics decide looks like a login-form field, explaining why neither WIP.39's `isTrusted` guard nor `autocomplete="off"` stopped it (both target other mechanisms — synthetic JS-dispatched events and the browser's separate form-field-history feature — not this).

Rewrote `_hardenFilterInputAgainstPasswordManagers()` into `_hardenFilterInputAgainstAutofill()`, adding two techniques specifically documented to defeat Chrome's own native credential-autofill (neither of which respects `autocomplete="off"`): (1) `type="search"` instead of `text` — Chrome's credential heuristic keys off `text`/`email`-type inputs, not `search`-type ones (also more semantically correct for a filter box); new CSS neutralizes the resulting native search-input chrome (rounded corners, native ✕ button) so the visual appearance is unchanged. (2) The field starts `readonly` and only becomes editable on a genuinely trusted `mousedown`/`focus` (gated on `event.isTrusted`, so it can't be defeated by a script/autofill mechanism synthetically dispatching those events either) — Chrome generally will not attempt to autofill a `readonly` field. The global filter's own auto-focus-after-render code (a PROGRAMMATIC, untrusted focus) now explicitly clears `.readOnly` itself right before focusing, since the trusted-only guard would otherwise leave it readonly (blocking the user's very next keystroke) until a second, real interaction. **Confirmed fixed by the user** on the real Chrome session that reproduced the bug.

'release-tracks': the yomo widget is still hidden (not removed, per WIP.38's revision) as a first layer of defense, though the newly-confirmed native-Chrome-autofill root cause means the widget's presence/absence was likely never the actual determining factor — kept regardless since it's still a reasonable, low-risk step and satisfies keeping the widget off the final rendered page.

The `readonly`-until-interaction trick (above) has a visible side effect: Chrome/Vivaldi paint their own default grey background on any `:read-only` input, so every column filter looked greyed-out until clicked at least once (reported by the user with a screenshot right after confirming the main fix). Added a `:read-only { background-color: #fff; }` CSS override for all three filter input types — lower specificity than the yellow `sa_col_filter_active_bg` inline style applied when a filter actually has a value, so an active filter still shows its yellow highlight correctly; only the idle/empty appearance was affected.

items: Found the REAL cause of the "tracklist not rendering with 'Batch Add Recording Aliases' active" report (WIP.38's widget removal, while still worth keeping, was not actually the fix): the "ISRCs" column filter was silently getting populated with the user's own MusicBrainz username ("vzell") the moment that other userscript activates, filtering every row out — the table WAS rendering, just with 0 visible rows after an unwanted filter, which looks identical to "nothing rendered" at a glance. Confirmed via a real browser console capture (`debug/fail.debug`): our own filter machinery logged `Column filter updated on column 19: "vzell"` — a legitimate-looking filter update, not a crash. No Chrome-style yellow `-webkit-autofill` highlight was visible on the field, ruling out Chrome's OWN native credential autofill specifically (that highlight is painted unconditionally via a UA stylesheet no page CSS can suppress) — but not third-party password-manager browser extensions, which insert values through their own content-script logic and don't necessarily show that highlight.

Hardened all three filter input types (global filter, per-column filter, per-sub-table filter) against exactly this class of interference, three layers deep: (1) their 'input' listeners now reject any event that is neither genuinely user-triggered (`event.isTrusted`, true only for real keystrokes/paste and for events some password-manager extensions and techniques like `document.execCommand('insertText', ...)` produce — impossible to spoof via a bare JS `dispatchEvent`) nor one of our own legitimate internal re-triggers (filter-history entries, "Clear ALL filters", a unique-values dropdown entry, the Unicode character picker — all of which now dispatch their synthetic 'input' events through a new shared `_dispatchInternalInputEvent()` helper that marks the event so it still passes) — any other 'input' event is dropped and the injected value discarded before it can silently activate as an active filter; (2) `autocomplete="off"` set on all three (none had it before); (3) the widely-recognized `data-lpignore`/`data-1p-ignore`/`data-bwignore`/`data-form-type="other"`/`data-protonpass-ignore` "leave this field alone" attributes (LastPass/1Password/Bitwarden/Dashlane/Proton Pass respectively) via a new shared `_hardenFilterInputAgainstPasswordManagers()` helper — these extensions frequently ignore `autocomplete="off"` on a target field by design (treating it as a common site-authoring mistake) but DO honor their own explicit opt-out markers.

Got the other userscript's actual source (`debug/other-userscript.js`) and confirmed it contains no code that reads/writes anything resembling a username, and never touches any element outside its own `#yomo-*` fields — ruling out its own JS as the direct writer. Revised theory: a password-manager extension targets `#yomo-src` (a fresh, unlabeled input that script adds near the top of the page) for autofill; WIP.38's `_removeYomoRecordingAliasesWidget()` used to `.remove()` that whole widget outright, and if an extension's fill attempt against `#yomo-src` gets interrupted by its removal, some extensions retry against a new nearby candidate once their original target vanishes — which could land on our column filter. Changed the function to HIDE the widget (`display: none`, DOM nodes kept, not removed) instead of deleting it, so any pending fill can complete harmlessly against a field nobody reads, rather than being forced to look elsewhere. Unconfirmed against a live password-manager extension — still being diagnosed with the user.

items: 'release-tracks': fixed the h2 "Credits" section (native `<div id="bottom-credits">`) still rendering AFTER the Tracklist section on the final page instead of before it, despite WIP.36's fix keeping its `<h3>` sub-headings intact. Root cause: `_relocateTrailingH2Sections()`'s whole-wrapper relocation (added in WIP.36) walked the Credits `<h2>` up to the first ancestor that is a direct child of `#content` and inserted it before the Tracklist `<h2>` — but on a real release page both the Tracklist and Credits sections share a common native `<div class="tracklist-and-credits">` wrapper several levels below `#content` (see `debug/credits.html`), so that walk produced `<div class="tracklist-and-credits">` itself — an ANCESTOR of the Tracklist `<h2>` it was about to be inserted before — throwing a DOM `HierarchyRequestError` that the function's own try/catch silently swallowed, aborting relocation for every trailing section, not just Credits. Now finds the lowest common ancestor ("LCA") the candidate `<h2>` actually shares with the Tracklist `<h2>` (rather than assuming it's always `#content`) and reorders siblings within that LCA instead — `<div id="bottom-credits">` now correctly moves as one intact unit to sit immediately before the Tracklist section.
