items: 'release-tracks': fixed the h2 "Credits" section on the final rendered page losing its native "Release"/"Release group" `<h3>` sub-headings (everything else inside — `table.details`, the release-group cover-art bigbox — stayed intact). Root cause 1: `renderGroupedTable()`'s initial-render cleanup pass swept EVERY `<h3>` on the page (not just the script's own generated `h3.mb-toggle-h3` section headers) before rebuilding, so the two native `<h3>` inside `<div id="bottom-credits">` were being deleted outright; now skipped via a targeted `el.closest('#bottom-credits')` guard alongside the existing `span.worklink` exception.

'release-tracks': fixed `_relocateTrailingH2Sections()` (which moves the native "Credits" `<h2>` to sit before the main Tracklist `<h2>` on the final page) tearing apart `<div id="bottom-credits">` in the process — it walked the Credits `<h2>`'s own `nextSibling` chain assuming the h2 was a direct child of `#content`, but the h2 is actually nested one level inside `#bottom-credits`, so its "siblings" were really `#bottom-credits`'s own children (`div#release-relationships`/`div#release-group-relationships`), which got individually re-parented onto `#content`, abandoning `#bottom-credits` empty. Now detects when the candidate h2 isn't a direct child of `#content` and relocates its whole wrapper element as one intact unit instead. See `debug/credits-original.html` / `debug/credits-final.html`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': before scraping a release's tracklist, now detects whether native per-track relationship credits (Recording engineer/Mixer/Engineer/Producer/Miscellaneous support) are currently rendered inline vs. consolidated into one combined block at the bottom of the page (MusicBrainz's own `#toggle-credits` control in `<span id="medium-toolbox">`, read via its own button label — "Display credits at bottom" means already inline, "Display credits inline" means currently at bottom), and if at bottom, clicks the control and awaits its re-render (`MutationObserver` on the button, idle-settle + 5s hard-timeout fallback, same shape as the existing overflow-tracks loader) before any row extraction runs — otherwise each row's own `dl.ars` credit block is missing/incomplete and the credit columns silently under-populate. See `debug/toolbox.org`.

'release-tracks': the native `<span id="medium-toolbox">` (toggle-credits/expand-all-mediums/collapse-all-mediums controls) is now stripped from the final rendered page via the existing `removeSelectors` mechanism, alongside the two other native `h2.tracklist` controls already removed there — its buttons re-render inert once the page has been restructured.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Reverted "Recording of work"'s attribute words (Acappella/Cover/Demo/Instrumental/Karaoke/Live/Medley/Partial) and "Recorded at place"'s "additional" attribute from their own separate columns (a word-per-column loop, and a standalone "Additional" column respectively) to render INLINE instead — the same `.mb-credit-attr` sentinel convention every `CREDIT_ROLES` column ("Engineer"/"Mixer"/etc.) already uses, e.g. "Rave On (live)" in "Recording of work", "Some Venue (additional)" appended to every place row in "Recorded at place" when a single relationship credits more than one place. Since the unique-values dropdown's per-attribute synthetic filter entries (WIP.32) already scan `.mb-credit-attr` generically with no column-name gating, both columns get that filtering — and its matching-text highlight (WIP.33) — for free, with zero new dropdown code. No more separate attribute-word/"Additional" columns to page-wide-gate, so that whole scan (`_presentRecOfAttributes`/`_pageHasRecordedAtPlaceAdditional`) was also removed.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Rows matching one of the new per-attribute/per-task synthetic dropdown filters (WIP.32) now get the exact matched string highlighted in the same color as any other active column filter — e.g. clicking "additional" in the "Engineer" column's dropdown highlights just the word "additional" inside each matching credit's parenthetical, not the whole cell or the whole `<li>`. A merged multi-person credit with several different attribute/task values in one cell only highlights the specific credit(s) whose own value actually matched.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added two more synthetic entries to the unique-values dropdown's "Cell structure" block, this time dynamic per-distinct-value filters rather than fixed checks: one entry per unique credit attribute word (e.g. "additional", "assistant", "co", "executive") and one per unique task string (e.g. "task: Second Engineer") actually present anywhere in a credit-role column's visible cells — e.g. the "Engineer" column on https://musicbrainz.org/release/6d19588c-0305-4fb0-b687-d4b75a75c3fd (`debug/unique-attribute-task.html`). Clicking one filters straight to every row where that specific attribute or task is credited, without typing free text. Attribute-word entries cover every credit-role column ("Recording engineer"/"Mixer"/"Engineer"/"Producer"/"Miscellaneous support") and "Produced for label"; task-value entries cover the 5 credit-role columns only ("Produced for label" has no task concept). `_buildCreditListItem`/`_buildLabelCreditListTd` now wrap attribute-word text in a `<span class="mb-credit-attr">` sentinel (and stamp the existing task `<i>` with `mb-credit-task`) so these values are reliably distinguishable from other free text sharing the same parenthetical; both new entry families reuse the exact `dataset.mbMultirowMode` → `testRowMatch()` plumbing every other synthetic entry in this block already uses, via a colon-prefixed compound mode string (`"attr:additional"`, `"task:task: Second Engineer"`) rather than a parallel filter mechanism.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added two new synthetic entries to the unique-values dropdown's optional "Cell structure" block, for additional structural filtering beyond plain text-value matching: "≠ track/recording name" for the "Title" column, matching rows where a third-party userscript (e.g. jesus2099's) has flagged the displayed track title as different from the underlying recording name — detected via the literal "≠" character in the title-anchor's own tooltip (`title="track name: …\n≠rec. name: …"`), immune to exactly which third-party script produced it; and "~ has name variation" for ANY column, matching rows where at least one credited entity (artist, label, place, …) uses a MusicBrainz `<span class="name-variation">` — the same alias/differently-spelled name rendered with a dotted underline on the live page (e.g. "Nassau Coliseum" in "Recorded at place", "Andres Bermudezat" in "Engineer"). Both entries appear even on columns that aren't otherwise collapsable (e.g. "Title"), showing a "Cell structure" header only when more than one synthetic entry would actually appear, matching the existing single-entry "○ empty cells" convention.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the "extracted column" header background (WIP.29) never actually appearing on release-tracks' AR-derived columns, despite being applied at `<th>`-creation time in `applyExtractTrackTitleData()`. Root cause: that function's `<th>`s are built during pre-processing against the NATIVE page's own table, BEFORE the real `table.tbl` this script renders even exists — only their text is scraped into the final header list, and those original DOM nodes are discarded, never reused, so styling them has no visible effect. This is the exact same underlying problem WIP.27 already diagnosed and fixed for the header glyph icons (`_initColHeaderGlyph()`), just not recognized as the same class of bug at the time. New `_stampArColumnHeaderBg(columnName)` mirrors `_initColHeaderGlyph()`'s already-proven approach: a post-render, by-name lookup against the actual rendered `table.tbl`, called from `renderGroupedTable()`'s tail alongside the glyph re-injection calls.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Every column release-tracks extracts from the Title cell's "ARs" data ("ARs"/"AcoustIDs"/"ISRCs", the "Recording of work"/"Recorded at" family and its attribute columns, and the engineer/mixer/producer/copyright credit columns) now gets the same header background color a generic synthetic column gets on other page types (`mb-extracted-column` + the existing `sa_ui_thead_th_extracted_bg` setting, default a greenish grey) instead of looking identical to the page's own native columns. "Video"/"Disambiguation"/"Recording artist" are unaffected — they're extracted from other parts of the Title/Artist cells, not from `dl.ars`.

The 📊 unique-values dropdown's flag-icon decoration (`sa_enable_dropdown_flag_icons` setting, existing feature already covering Country/Area/Locality/Region/Location/Place/Country-Date columns) now also covers release-tracks' "Recorded at place" column — each dropdown entry gets the same region/country flag icons shown in the table cell itself. No new icon-scanning logic was needed: "Recorded at place" cells already use the identical ``/`` shapes the existing scan already recognizes; the column just needed to be added to the column-name allow-list.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the credit-role columns ("Recording engineer"/"Mixer"/"Engineer"/"Producer"/"Miscellaneous support") silently dropping a credited artist's `<span class="comment">` disambiguation note entirely — e.g. a name-variation-wrapped credit's "primary alias" cross-reference (`debug/artist-name-variation-and-primary-alias.html`: "Louis Lehav" crediting engineer, with a `(Louis Lahav)` note pointing at the artist's primary alias) rendered as just the bare name, with the note gone. `_findCreditSegmentTextAnnotation` only reads a segment's own TEXT nodes, but this note's parenthesis characters live inside the `<span class="comment">` element itself, not as sibling text, so it was invisible to that lookup. New `_findCreditSegmentCommentSpan` finds this element (also covers a plain artist disambiguation with no name-variation, e.g. "Clarence Clemons (American saxophonist)") and clones it verbatim right after the artist anchor, independent of the existing attribute/instrument/task parenthetical.

Fixed a name-variation-wrapped credit (e.g. "Louis Lehav" above) losing its underline styling once extracted, even though the text/link itself was already correct — MusicBrainz underlines a `<span class="name-variation">`-wrapped credit via that span's own CSS class, to visually flag it as an alias rather than the artist's primary name, but the credit-role columns only ever cloned the bare `<a>` inside it, discarding the wrapper. `_buildCreditListItem` ("Recording engineer"/"Mixer"/"Engineer"/"Producer"/"Miscellaneous support") and the "Recorded at event" cell builder both now clone the wrapping `<span class="name-variation">` instead of the bare anchor whenever the credited artist/event uses one.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Renamed the "Recording of" column to "Recording of work" and "Produced for" to "Produced for label" (glyphs unchanged) — clarifies what each column actually links to.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "Produced for" column to `release-tracks`, extracted from each track's "produced for:" relationship (`debug/copyright.html`'s "Laurel Canyon Ltd." example) — labels only, optionally prefixed with "co"/"executive" attribute words rendered inline after the label's name (e.g. "Laurel Canyon Ltd. (executive)"), matching the credit-role columns' own attribute convention. Reuses the existing `sa_enable_release_tracks_credit_role_columns` setting; positioned after both "Phonographic copyright" columns, still before "ARs".

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed "Phonographic copyright (℗) by label" (WIP.26) never appearing at all, even on a release with real label credits for it (`debug/greetings-original.html`). MusicBrainz can render a track's ARs as multiple SIBLING `<dl class="ars">` blocks inside the same bare `div.ars` — one `<dl>` crediting an artist directly, followed by a separate sibling `<dl>` crediting labels, both using the exact same `<dt>phonographic copyright (℗) by:</dt>` phrase. The lookup used a first-match-only `.find()`, so every `<dt>` after the first (the label one, in this case) was silently dropped, both in the page-wide "does this column exist" gate and in the per-row cell builder. It now collects every matching `<dt>` across every sibling `<dl>` and merges their `<dd>`s, mirroring `_findCreditDts`'s own "collect every match" convention (which was never `.find()`-based and so was unaffected by this bug).

Fixed every credit-role column header ("Recording engineer", "Mixer", "Engineer", "Producer", "Miscellaneous support") and both "Phonographic copyright" headers (WIP.26) never actually showing MusicBrainz's marker glyph, despite that being WIP.26's stated intent (`debug/greetings-rendered.html`). The glyph `<span>` was appended directly to the `<th>` at creation time, but `makeTableSortableUnified()` unconditionally rebuilds every `<th>` from a plain `textContent` string shortly after (as part of the existing sort-icon/unique-value-count UI setup), discarding any child element added before that point — the same root cause already diagnosed and fixed for "Recording of"'s own glyph in an earlier session. The glyph is now injected post-render by the existing `_initColHeaderGlyph()` helper instead, called from `renderGroupedTable()`'s tail alongside the pre-existing "Recording of"/"Recorded at event"/"Recorded at place" calls — the established, already-working pattern for this exact problem, which this feature should have reused from the start.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items:
Fixed the "Recorded at place" column (WIP.14/WIP.17) rendering MusicBrainz's empty `` glyph marker in front of every place, once per list item (`debug/place-icon.html`) — redundant since that same glyph is already shown once in the column header. The marker is used purely to detect where each place's own content starts (`_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd`'s per-place segmentation), but was also being appended as part of that segment's content into the rendered `
  • `. It's now dropped as soon as it's used as a segment boundary, never appended to the cell. No other content changes — area chains, flags, instrument attributions, and multi-place splitting are all unaffected.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the "Engineer"/"Mixer" (and any other pair of) credit columns rendering empty for a track whose `<dt>` credits the same artists under multiple roles at once, e.g. `<dt>engineer and mixer:</dt>` (`debug/Nightshift.html`) — the whole `<dt>` was matched as one unit against a single role's `roleWords`, so `"engineer and mixer:"` matched neither the bare "engineer" role (trailing word is "mixer", not "engineer") nor the "mixer" role (leading words "engineer and" aren't recognized attribute words), leaving both columns empty despite ARs clearly crediting both. `_findCreditDts` now splits each `<dt>`'s body into role components on `,`/` and ` (the same separators MusicBrainz uses to join multiple artists in a `<dd>`) before matching, so `"engineer and mixer:"` → `["engineer", "mixer"]`, each checked independently — the same `<dd>`'s artists now correctly appear in BOTH "Engineer" and "Mixer". A `<dt>` with no `,`/` and ` (the common case) splits into one component, so single-role credits are completely unaffected; the per-component attribute-word strictness (e.g. "recording engineer" still never matching bare "engineer") is unchanged, just applied per component instead of to the whole `<dt>`.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Reverted the per-role attribute-word columns (e.g. "Mixer (Assistant)") added in WIP.16. A credited artist's own attribute words (Additional/Assistant/Associate/Co/Executive) now render inline right after their name, inside the role's own column, instead of as a separate page-wide-gated column per attribute word — e.g. the "Mixer" cell now shows a two-item list "Paul Hamingson (assistant)" / "Bob Clearmountain" instead of a flag in a separate "Mixer (Assistant)" column (`debug/attributes.html`). Applies to every credit-role column that can have attribute words: "Recording engineer", "Mixer", "Engineer", "Producer". `_creditRoleState`'s page-wide attribute-word union tracking, and the header/row-population code that built one `<th>`/`<td>` per attribute word, are removed — the page-wide scan now only needs to know WHICH roles are used anywhere on the release, not which attribute words.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: When a credited artist has both attribute words and an instrument/task/other annotation, both now render together in one parenthetical, comma-separated, e.g. "Karl Egsieker (assistant/co, task: Second Engineer)" instead of the attribute words being dropped from the artist's own list item entirely (they only ever showed up in the now-removed separate attribute column). Multiple attribute words on one credit are joined with "/", matching the order they appear in `attributeVocab` (e.g. "assistant/co").

Any per-artist annotation whose text starts with "task:" (case-insensitive — MusicBrainz's own "miscellaneous support:" wording, but the same check applies to a task annotation on any other credit role too) now renders in italics, e.g. "Sandy Park (task: string contractor)" with the task text italicized. Every other annotation kind (a linked instrument, or other free text like "other vocals [...]") stays plain, unchanged from WIP.20/WIP.22.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the credit-role columns (WIP.16/WIP.20/WIP.21) silently dropping a credited artist's own parenthetical note whenever it's free text rather than a linked instrument or the specific "(task: …)" wording — e.g. a bare "engineer:" credit's "(other vocals [Sam Moore vocal])" note (`debug/missing-engineer.html`/`debug/soul-days.html`) rendered as a bare artist name with the note gone. `_findCreditSegmentTaskAnnotation` (WIP.21, matched only `(task: …)`) is replaced by `_findCreditSegmentTextAnnotation`, which matches ANY `(…)` parenthetical across the segment's text nodes rather than special-casing each wording MusicBrainz happens to use — still only consulted when no instrument anchor was found in the segment, so it can't shadow the instrument case. "(task: string contractor)" still renders exactly as before; "(other vocals [Sam Moore vocal])" now renders too.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items:
Fixed a bare "engineer:" (and any other) credit column (WIP.16/WIP.20) silently dropping an artist entirely whenever MusicBrainz wraps that artist's anchor in `…` (an alias/disambiguated name), instead of just that one artist's instrument/task annotation being lost. `_buildCreditListTd`'s per-artist segmentation looked for the artist `` only as a direct child of the segment; a name-variation-wrapped artist's only direct child is the wrapping ``, so that segment produced no `
  • ` at all — e.g. a bare "engineer:" crediting 3 artists where the first is name-variation-wrapped rendered only the other 2, with the first missing without any indication. New `_findCreditSegmentArtistAnchor`/`_findCreditSegmentInstrumentAnchors` now search each segment node's descendants too (not just the node itself), mirroring WIP.15's identical `_recordedAtDdAnchor` fix for the same name-variation-nesting problem in "Recorded at place".

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "Miscellaneous support" credit column, extracted from `<dt>miscellaneous support:</dt>` the same way as the other 4 credit-role columns (WIP.16), reusing `CREDIT_ROLES`/`_findCreditDts`/`_buildCreditListTd` with an empty `attributeVocab` (no attribute-word prefix is recognized for this role, so it gets no attribute columns). Each credited artist is paired with their own task annotation when MusicBrainz provides one — rendered as plain parenthetical text, not a link, e.g. "(task: string contractor)" — via new `_findCreditSegmentTaskAnnotation`, appended the same way the instrument annotation already is for the other 4 roles, so an artist with a task reads as "Sandy Park (task: string contractor)". Gated by the same `sa_enable_release_tracks_credit_role_columns` setting as the other 4 credit-role columns; positioned last in that group, still before "Recorded at place"/"ARs".

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items:
Fixed the "Recording engineer"/"Mixer"/"Engineer"/"Producer" credit columns (WIP.16) turning a credited instrument into a spurious extra list item instead of keeping it attached to the artist it belongs to. MusicBrainz renders a per-artist instrument attribution as " (strings)" right after that artist's own anchor — the previous implementation flattened every `` inside the `
` (both artist AND instrument anchors) into one `
  • ` each, so e.g. 3 credited engineers each with an instrument attribution rendered as 6 list items ("Ian Kagey", "strings", "Rob Lebret", "strings", …) instead of 3 ("Ian Kagey (strings)", "Rob Lebret (strings)", …). `_buildCreditListTd` now segments each `
    ` structurally on its own `` marker (mirroring "Recorded at place"'s (WIP.17) `span.placelink`-marker segmentation) so any instrument anchor found within an artist's own segment is appended to that artist's `
  • ` as " (strings)" instead of becoming its own item. Multiple instrument anchors within one artist's segment (e.g. "(guitar, bass)") are all kept, comma-joined — untested against real data, no such example found in any debug snapshot.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added support for individual ISRC pages (/isrc/<code>, e.g. /isrc/USSM19500019), new pageType 'isrc'. The native page already renders a fixed, fully-populated `<table class="tbl mergeable-table">` (checkbox / Title / Artist / Length) directly below its own correct `<h1>`/`<h2>`, so the new page definition needs no listToTable/insertH2/renameH2ToH3 and no fetch pagination (`non_paginated: true`) — mirrors the existing 'cd-stub'/'auto-editor-election' page definitions. Title's native `.comment` disambiguation span (often live-performance metadata, e.g. "live, 1975-10-18, early show: The Roxy Theatre, West Hollywood, CA, USA") is split into a synthetic Comment column via `extractMainColumn: 'Title'`, then further parsed by the existing `eventParts` extractor into Event-Type/Event-Date/Event-Detail/Event-Venue/Event-Venue-Detail/Event-City/Event-State/Event-Country/Event-Additional-Info columns — the same convention already used by 'work-recordings-filtered' and others. Artist's native multi-artist-credit markup is handled by the existing generic column pipeline with no new extractor; Length uses the standard `integerColumns` mm:ss sort convention. The native checkbox `<th>` carries no `checkbox-cell` CSS class (unlike other MusicBrainz merge-tables), so a small pageType==='isrc'-scoped pre-processing step stamps that class on before the header scan runs, letting the existing `sa_remove_checkbox_cell` setting govern it exactly like every other merge-checkbox column, without introducing a new removal mechanism.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added an "Additional" column, right before "Recorded at place", for that relationship's own "additional" attribute — MusicBrainz renders it as the adverb "additionally recorded at:" (confirmed via the embedded relationship-type metadata on the edit-relationships page; unlike the engineer/mixer/producer credit columns' adjective "additional recording engineer:" wording), shown here as the canonical word "additional" when present, empty otherwise, matching every other attribute column's convention. "Recorded at event" gets no equivalent column — its own "additional" attribute is never actually rendered in that direction by MusicBrainz. No real-data example of this attribute exists in any captured snapshot; verified via a synthetic jsdom test against the confirmed MB relationship-type template only.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: "Recorded at place" (WIP.14/WIP.15) now renders as a collapsible multi-row list when a single "recorded at:" relationship credits more than one place (e.g. a track recorded partly at one studio and partly at another) — one `<li>` per place, each with its own full "in <area>, <area>, <country>" chain and flags, instead of previously running every place's content together into one unreadable flat cell. Splitting is structural (a new place starts at each place's own leading glyph marker in the source markup), not by reading the "and"/"," separator text, so it's immune to wording variations. Per-place extra context (e.g. an "(<instrument>)" attribution noting which instrument was recorded at that specific place) is preserved on the correct place's row; only the literal "and"/"," joining two places is dropped. Single-place rows are unaffected in content (still exactly the place + its area chain), just now wrapped in a one-item list like every other collapsible column in this family — no behavior change for the common case.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added "Recording engineer", "Mixer", "Engineer", and "Producer" credit columns to `release-tracks`, extracted from the same bare `div.ars` as "Recording of"/"Recorded at" (WIP.13/WIP.14), sourced from sibling `<dl class="ars"><dt>recording engineer:</dt>`/`<dt>mixer:</dt>`/`<dt>engineer:</dt>`/`<dt>producer:</dt>` relationships. Each role can be prefixed with attribute words (Additional, Assistant, Associate, Co, and — Engineer/Producer only — Executive); one column per attribute word actually used on the release is added per role, header-prefixed with the role's own label to avoid collisions (e.g. "Mixer (Assistant)"), showing the attribute word when present, empty otherwise — mirrors the existing "Recording of" attribute-column pattern. When a `<dd>` credits multiple artists (comma/"and"-joined), the cell renders as a collapsible multi-row list, reusing the existing `_findCellListItems`/`initCollapsableColumns` machinery with zero new wiring. Gated by a new dedicated setting, `sa_enable_release_tracks_credit_role_columns` (default on), independent of the existing "Recording of"/"Recorded at" toggle. Positioned after "Recorded at place", still directly before "ARs", which is left completely unchanged as always.

When a track has more than one matching credit for the same role (confirmed in real data: a track with both a bare `<dt>mixer:</dt>` and a separate `<dt>assistant mixer:</dt>`), all matching credits are MERGED into one multi-person list for that role's column, rather than keeping only the first match in document order (the convention every other column in this family uses) — no credited person is silently dropped from a column literally named after their role. Attribute columns become row-level "was this attribute used by any of the merged entries" flags rather than tied to one specific person.

The bare `<dt>engineer:</dt>` role is disambiguated from the compound `<dt>recording engineer:</dt>` role via a strict prefix-word check (every word before the matched role phrase must itself be a recognized attribute word, or the whole `<dt>` is rejected for that role) — a lenient check (silently dropping unrecognized words, like the existing "Recording of" attribute parser does) would wrongly accept "recording engineer:" as a bare "engineer" credit too, since its last word literally is "engineer:". Word-splitting uses `/[\s-]+/` (whitespace OR hyphen), not just whitespace, since MusicBrainz hyphen-attaches the "co" attribute to the following word (e.g. "co-recording engineer:") — confirmed only in the spec examples (`debug/artist-roles.org`), no real-data example of any hyphenated-prefix or "co"/"executive"/"additional"/"associate" combo exists in `debug/full.html`, so this path is unit-tested synthetically only, not against real MusicBrainz markup.

Trailing dates on these credits (e.g. "(on 1975-10-18)", "(in 2015)") are dropped entirely — unlike "Recording of", which has its own "Recording date" column, these 4 roles get no equivalent; the date stays visible in "ARs" only. Achieved for free since only `<a>` anchors are ever extracted, never trailing text/comment nodes.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "Recorded at place" (WIP.14) now includes the following "in <area>, <area>, <country>" chain (area links, region-flag image, CSS-flag-background country span) alongside the place link itself, instead of just the bare venue name — e.g. "Meadowlands Arena" now also shows "in East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States" with both flags. "Recorded at event" is unchanged: its own anchor text already spells out date/venue/location, so no area chain is added there. Both cells still drop the trailing " (on YYYY-MM-DD)" (stays in "ARs" only, same as before).

Fixed "Recorded at place"/"Recorded at event" extracting nothing at all for tracks whose place/event has a name-variation (an alias name differing from the entity's canonical one — MusicBrainz wraps the link one level deeper as `...` in that case, mirroring the Title cell's own name-variation markup). The anchor lookup was scoped to `:scope > a`, a direct-child-only query that silently found nothing once the anchor sat inside that extra ``; relaxed to search any depth, since the href-prefix filter (`/place/` vs. `/event/`, disjoint from area links' `/area/`) already picks the right anchor unambiguously regardless of nesting.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added "Recorded at event" and "Recorded at place" columns to `release-tracks`, extracted from the same bare `div.ars`'s sibling `<dl class="ars"><dt>recorded at:</dt>...</dl>` relationship (a sibling of "recording of:", not nested inside it) already partly covered by the "Recording of" feature. MusicBrainz's `<dt>` wording for this relationship varies (`"recorded at:"`, `"recorded at and mixed at:"`, other "mixed at" combinations), so classification is instead by the `<dd>`'s leading native glyph span — `span.eventlink` vs. `span.placelink` — matched via a loose case-insensitive `"recorded at"` substring test against the `<dt>` rather than an exact/anchored pattern. Two separate columns (not one shared "Recorded at") because the standard sort/filter header pipeline derives each column's identity fresh from its header text on every render — two headers both showing literal "Recorded at" would collide and the second would never be created. Cell value is just the cloned event/place link (no "in <area>, <area>, <country>" chain, no trailing date — no date extraction this round, deferred). A row with more than one "recorded at" entry of the same kind only yields the first, in document order. Reuses the existing `sa_enable_release_tracks_recording_of_columns` setting (label/description updated) rather than adding a new one — same purely-additive family. Positioned after "Recording date", still directly before "ARs"; "ARs" itself is left completely untouched, same contract as "Recording of".

Generalized the post-render column-header glyph injector (`_recOfInitColHeaderGlyph` → `_initColHeaderGlyph(columnName, glyphClass)`) so the same technique now serves all three glyph columns ("Recording of"/`worklink`, "Recorded at event"/`eventlink`, "Recorded at place"/`placelink`) instead of duplicating the function body. The `height`/`margin` CSS fixes already established for `worklink` (see WIP.13) are reused as-is for the two new glyph classes, since the root cause — any direct child of `.mb-col-hdr-flex`, a flex container, gets its outer display blockified regardless of its own `display` value — is unrelated to the specific glyph class; this is however **unverified in a live browser** for `eventlink`/`placelink` and may need the same kind of Computed-panel comparison `worklink` needed if either icon turns out missing, mis-sized, or misaligned.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items:
Added a new "Recording of " column (label includes MusicBrainz's own empty, CSS-styled work-glyph icon, matching the convention it's always shown with) to `release-tracks`, extracted from the "ARs" relationship data's `
recording of:
Work Name...
` block (see e.g. `/release/6d19588c-0305-4fb0-b687-d4b75a75c3fd`'s DVD-Video medium) — keeps the work link, same as every other entity reference extracted this session. Also adds one column per recording attribute actually used somewhere on the release (`Acappella`, `Cover`, `Demo`, `Instrumental`, `Karaoke`, `Live`, `Medley`, `Partial` — MusicBrainz prefixes the `
` with these, e.g. `"live cover recording of:"`), showing the attribute name itself when present (e.g. "live") and an empty cell when absent. Both gated by the existing page-wide "only render when at least one track has a value" pattern, plus a new master setting `sa_enable_release_tracks_recording_of_columns` (default **on**) for the whole feature. Positioned directly before "ARs" (not chained after Title like every other column added this session), attribute columns first, then "Recording of", then "Recording date" (see below).

Unlike every prior extraction this session, this one is purely additive: the work link is *cloned*, and the "ARs" column's underlying `div.ars` content is never touched, removed, or modified — "ARs" keeps showing the exact same full relationship data (work link included, now duplicated) it always has. Per explicit instruction, since the source `dl.ars`'s `<dd>` also holds nested writer/lyricist/publisher `dl.ars` blocks that have no column of their own and must not be lost.

Fixed the "Recording of" column's work-glyph icon not actually appearing in the rendered header — the column's `<th>` is later completely rebuilt from a plain text string by the standard sort/filter header pipeline, which destroys any child element appended to it beforehand. The glyph is now injected afterward instead, mirroring the same established pattern already used for the CAA/EAA column-header thumbnail toggle button. A second issue then surfaced: the glyph element existed in the DOM but stayed invisible, because any direct child of a flex container (`.mb-col-hdr-flex`) has its `display` forced to a block type by the CSS spec regardless of its own `display` value, which strips the line-height-derived height an inline icon normally gets from its native, non-flex context — a childless block box with no explicit height is just 0px tall. Fixed by giving the injected glyph an explicit height. A third issue then surfaced: a trailing space text node after the glyph (added so it wouldn't sit flush against the sort icons) turned out not to survive CSS whitespace-collapsing between two flex-blockified siblings — replaced with an explicit `margin-right` on the glyph itself, which isn't subject to that collapsing. A fourth, mirror-image issue then surfaced on the OTHER side of the glyph: the leading space already baked into the header template's text node (`"Recording of "`) collapses for the identical reason, leaving no gap between the label and the glyph — fixed the same way, with an explicit `margin-left` on the glyph.

Added a new "Recording date" column to `release-tracks`, positioned directly after "Recording of", extracting the optional `(on YYYY-MM-DD)` date MusicBrainz appends after the work link in the same "recording of" `<dd>` (e.g. "(on 1978-07-07)" → "1978-07-07") — same purely-additive/page-wide-gated pattern as "Recording of" itself, under the same `sa_enable_release_tracks_recording_of_columns` master setting.

Reordered the whole "Recording of"/"Recording date"/attribute-column group: the attribute columns (`Acappella`/`Cover`/…/`Partial`) now come first, followed by "Recording of", then "Recording date", then "ARs" — previously "Recording of" and (then-named) "Date" preceded the attribute columns. Renamed "Date" to "Recording date" at the same time, since a bare "Date" read ambiguously next to the release-level tracklist.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: `release-tracks`' "Disambiguation" column no longer keeps the literal `(`/`)` MusicBrainz wraps the comment's text in (e.g. "(version 1)" → "version 1", "(live, 1978‐07‐07: …)" → "live, 1978‐07‐07: …") — redundant once the comment has its own dedicated column. New `_stripSurroundingParens()` helper strips a leading `(`/trailing `)` from the cell's first/last actual text node via a `TreeWalker`, handling both structural shapes the comment can appear in (bare text directly in `span.comment`, or wrapped in a nested `<bdi>`).
`release-tracks`' `integerColumns` now also center-aligns (`align: 'C'`) the native `#` track-number column, matching `Rating`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the overflow-tracklist progress bar (WIP.9) only ever showing its static initial "medium 1 of 1..." text with no fill, instead of live progress. It was previously only updated once a medium fully finished loading — for the common case of a single overflowing medium (often the release's ONLY one), that meant the bar showed nothing but the initial text for the entire load (which can itself take as long as a whole paginated fetch), then flashed a completed state for a moment before the next phase's progress bar overwrote it. Now updates live as each medium's own AJAX response streams rows in, reusing the same `MutationObserver` that already detects completion — fill percentage, track count, and the remaining-time estimate all progress continuously during a medium's own load, not just between mediums.

Fixed the same progress bar's label text getting clipped on both ends (e.g. "Loading" losing its "Load") — its container's `min-width` (420px) was sized for the original, shorter paginated-fetch label and never grows to fit longer content since its fill/label children are both `position:absolute` and so don't contribute to the container's own auto width. Bumped to 600px, comfortably fitting the overflow-tracks label's worst case (~73 characters) while staying under the existing 750px cap.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: `release-tracks`' "Disambiguation" column is no longer unconditional — it's now only created once at least one track on the release has the parenthetical comment, same page-wide decision as "Video"/"Recording artist" (`renderGroupedTable()`'s shared header template forces this to be decided once across the whole release, not per medium). "AcoustIDs"/"ISRCs" deliberately keep their current behavior (created whenever their setting is on, independent of whether data is present yet) — their data arrives via an async third-party lookup that's often still in progress when this script runs, which is exactly why the late-arrival `MutationObserver` (added earlier this session) exists; gating their column creation on data already being present would make that observer's job impossible most of the time, since it has nowhere to place data once its destination column doesn't exist.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a progress indicator for `release-tracks`' "Load all tracks..." overflow handling (`loadAllOverflowMediumTracks`), reusing the same inline progress bar the paginated-fetch loop already shows ("Loading page X of Y... (Z rows) - Ns left"). On a release with several overflowing mediums (each its own AJAX round trip that can take a few seconds), this phase previously ran silently before the real fetch loop even started, which could look like a hang. Now shows "Loading overflow tracks: medium X of Y... (Z tracks) - Ns left", updated once per medium (not continuously during each medium's own wait).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items:
Added a new "Recording artist" column to `release-tracks`, extracted from the native `
Recording artist: …joined artist links…
` MusicBrainz glomms into the Title cell when a track's recording is credited to a different artist than the release itself (e.g. a live cover, a guest performance — see e.g. the "2 - DVD-Video" medium on `/release/6d19588c-0305-4fb0-b687-d4b75a75c3fd`). The whole `` — preserving every joined artist link and join phrase verbatim, same reasoning as the release-level Artist backfill — is moved (not cloned) into the new column. Like "Video", the column's presence is decided once, page-wide (any track on the release has the credit), not per medium, since `renderGroupedTable()`'s single shared header template would otherwise silently drop a `` present on only some mediums' native theads. Positioned directly after "Artist" — the release-level credit reads first, with the recording's own (possibly different) credit immediately beside it.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Renamed `release-tracks`' (WIP.4) "AcoustID"/"ISRC" columns to "AcoustIDs"/"ISRCs" (plural, since each cell can hold more than one entry).

Added a new, conditionally-created "Video" column to `release-tracks`, extracted from the native `<span class="video" title="This recording is a video">` icon MusicBrainz glomms into the Title cell for video recordings (see e.g. the "2 - DVD-Video" medium on `/release/6d19588c-0305-4fb0-b687-d4b75a75c3fd`) — reuses the existing, generic `ColumnDataExtractor.video` extractor (already used by several other pageTypes, e.g. `artist-recordings`, via a normal `columnExtractors` entry) rather than duplicating its move-the-span/audio-video-sort-key logic. Unlike a normal `columnExtractors` entry, which always creates its synthetic column, the "Video" `<th>` is only added when at least one track ANYWHERE ON THE RELEASE (any medium) has the icon, so a release with no video tracks at all never gets a permanently empty column — decided once, page-wide, not per medium: `renderGroupedTable()` builds a single header `<thead>` template from the first `table.tbl` in the document and clones it for every medium, so a `<th>` present on only some mediums' native theads would silently vanish from every rendered table (row data still carries through per group, the header does not). Positioned directly after "Title" (before "Disambiguation").

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a new (default on) `sa_enable_release_tracks_acoustid_isrc_observer` setting: a `MutationObserver`-based reactive fix for the "AcoustID"/"ISRC" columns (WIP.4) so late-arriving data from a third-party userscript's async AcoustID lookup (e.g. jesus2099's, a network round-trip to acoustid.org per recording — routinely still in progress by the time this script's own one-shot extraction pass ran) reaches those columns instead of being silently missed. Watches each medium's table for AcoustID/ISRC data appearing after the fact and relocates it into the right column reactively, mirroring the existing area-flag/region-correction observer (`initAreaFlagRegionObserver`). Only does anything when at least one of the AcoustID/ISRC column settings is on; zero overhead otherwise. Required switching `applyExtractTrackTitleData()`'s Title-cell cleanup from cloning the recording link/ARs/AcoustID/ISRC content to *moving* it — a clone would silently break this fix, since whatever the decorating userscript is tracking (a live object reference, or a re-query matching the same class/attributes) needs the actual live node to still be present in the rendered table for its own late decoration to land anywhere this observer can see it.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the "ARs"/"AcoustID"/"ISRC" columns (WIP.4) never getting a collapse toggle on any release-tracks page with more than one medium, even when a cell's content clearly overflowed the clamp. Root cause: `renderGroupedTable()`'s `shouldStayOpen` heuristic (which decides whether a sub-table starts expanded or `display:none`) only recognizes a lone sub-table or the literal categories `album`/`official` — release-tracks' medium-title categories ("1 - CD", "2 - DVD-Video", …) matched neither, so every medium on a multi-medium release started hidden. `initCollapsableColumns()`/`makeColumnsResizable()` then ran immediately afterward against that still-hidden table — measuring `scrollHeight`/`clientHeight` on a `display:none` element always reads 0 in a real browser, so the overflow check permanently found nothing to add a toggle to, even after the section was later expanded by hand. This bug predates this session but was invisible until `collapsableColumns` was added to release-tracks in WIP.4. Fixed by keeping every release-tracks sub-table expanded by default regardless of medium count — matching the feature's whole point (consolidating a release's tracklists into one always-visible view) and avoiding the hidden-at-measurement-time trap entirely.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: `release-tracks`' "Title" column no longer shows the raw glommed cell MusicBrainz (and, once it has run, the third-party jesus2099 "SUPER MIND CONTROL" script) builds it from — just the clean track title now. Everything else that used to be crammed into that cell is extracted into its own new column: a "Disambiguation" column (the parenthetical comment shown when a track's title differs from its recording, e.g. "(live, 1978‐07‐07: The Roxy Theatre, West Hollywood, CA, USA)"); an always-present, collapsible "ARs" column at the end of the table (the recording's general relationships — engineer, producer, recording-of-work, publisher, … — previously glommed into the Title cell as a `<div class="ars">`), with its own independent collapse-height settings (`sa_enable_ars_collapse`, `sa_ars_column_max_height_em`, `sa_ars_column_max_width`) rather than sharing the "Annotation" column's; and two new off-by-default multi-row columns, "AcoustID" and "ISRC" (`sa_enable_release_tracks_acoustid_column` / `sa_enable_release_tracks_isrc_column`), each entry rendered as its own list row instead of one long comma-separated line — AcoustID entries keep their native ×/+ link/unlink action link. The secondary "recording name" line MusicBrainz shows under a track's title when it differs from the underlying recording's name is dropped (not kept in any column, per explicit confirmation). Implemented via a new `applyExtractTrackTitleData()` DOM-surgery pass (mirroring the existing Artist-column backfill's approach) rather than the additive `columnExtractors` mechanism, since cleaning the Title cell in place isn't something that mechanism supports.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed `release-tracks`' backfilled "Artist" column (WIP.1) truncating a multi-artist release credit down to just the first artist — e.g. a release credited to "Bruce Springsteen & The E Street Band" rendered as just "Bruce Springsteen" in every row. `applyNormalizeMediumTracklists()` was capturing and cloning only the first `<a href="/artist/...">` found inside `p.subheader`'s `<bdi>`, dropping the join text (" & ", ", ", " feat. ", …) and any subsequent artist links; it now captures and clones the entire `<bdi>` artist-credit element, matching how MusicBrainz's own native Various-Artists per-track Artist cells already render multi-artist credits.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed `release-tracks`' "Load all tracks..." overflow handling (WIP.1) resolving after only a few milliseconds and still rendering the truncated 100-row tracklist: MusicBrainz replaces the triggering `<tr>` with a loading placeholder almost instantly on click, long before the AJAX response with the real rows has arrived, so waiting for that `<tr>` to leave the DOM (the original signal) fired a false-positive completion. `loadAllOverflowMediumTracks()` now parses the expected final track count from the overflow message ("...out of 1209 total.") and waits for the `<tbody>`'s actual data-row count to reach it, falling back to an idle-mutation heuristic only when that count can't be parsed; the per-medium timeout was also raised from 15s to 30s to give large tracklists room to load.

Fixed jesus2099 "SUPER MIND CONTROL" hover-toolzone artifacts (Merge/Edit/Open-edits quick-action `<div>`s, e.g. `<div class="jesus2099userjs81127toolzone" style="display:block">`) being cloned into the final rendered Length column with a baked-in `display:block` from whatever hover state was active at scrape time. Added a new generic `'jesus2099-any'` `columnErasers` sentinel (removes any element whose class starts with "jesus2099userjs", by prefix rather than one hardcoded suffix, since that userscript embeds an install/version-specific numeric ID) alongside the existing exact-class `'jesus2099'` sentinel, and applied it to `release-tracks`' Length column.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a new `release-tracks` pageType for bare release pages (musicbrainz.org/release/<mbid>), consolidating every medium's native tracklist into the standard filterable/sortable multi-table view via a new "Show all Tracks for Release" button (gated by the new `sa_enable_release_tracks` setting, default on). Each medium's `<thead>`-embedded title (e.g. "1 - CD") is synthesized into a sibling `<h3>` so the existing release-group h3-sibling-walk grouping pipeline can be reused unmodified; the native `<tr class="subh">` header row is promoted into a proper `<thead>`; an `Artist` column is always present, backfilled with the release's main artist credit on non-Various-Artists releases. Mediums truncated by MusicBrainz's own "Load all tracks..." overflow link (>100 tracks) are auto-loaded and awaited before the tracklist is scraped, so no tracks are missed. The native "Edit recording comments" button and settings-icon are stripped from the reused `h2.tracklist` header once it becomes the global filter/master-toggle anchor. Also adds a new additive `features.removeSelectors` (plural array) post-render step alongside the existing singular `removeSelector`.
